title: Harden the differential tier
description: JS-064's review backlog, closed before later tasks lean on the tier. A request meant to return rows asserts 200 and a non-empty answer, so a fixture or route broken on both servers can't pass. Timestamps are masked only where they change from run to run (DateCreated, LastPlayedDate, session times), so PremiereDate and similar stable dates are compared. A pinned (ids) entry that no longer matches fails, and is no longer reported as stale. acceptance.sh runs from a git-archive export, and its leak check counts only the containers of its own runs.
acceptanceCriteria: A request marked as returning rows fails the tier when both servers answer an error or an empty list, shown by a test
A wrong PremiereDate on jellyscale fails the tier; masked timestamp keys are listed in one place and documented
A pinned entry whose list changed fails without a contradictory 'no longer differs' note
acceptance.sh passes from a git-archive export and is not failed by a concurrent run.sh on the same host
source: JS-064 review backlog (QA and adversarial, build workflow 2026-11-07)
notes: Every later protocol task loops against this tier, so a false pass here is costly.
